discretion: A screenshot proves the walk ran, not that it shows the claim. The reviewer judges the visible claim and source mapping; rendered-state assertions grow row by row in the agent tests. No-feature-impact reasons are declarations for review, not proof.
unmapped_instruction: add a row or declare no feature impact (give a reason for each path)

FL-002.label: Memory units have a length cap; a memory over the cap is shortened to fit as one memory, and it is split only when it holds more than one distinct fact, with the split logged.
FL-002.walk: Save a fact over the cap: the same prompt runs again with 'this memory is too long, break it down into finer pieces' until every piece fits and stands alone (up to three rounds); a single fact is never refused as several, and nothing is dropped silently — the original stays in the journal.

FL-005.label: Duplicate detection at creation, and outright removal of deprecated memories so they never collide with new ones.
FL-005.walk: `/remember` the same fact twice; the second is caught as a duplicate rather than stored again.

FL-015.label: Constitution: Typed edges between memories (merged from, supersedes, contradicts, and richer kinds at creation and curation) with a depth-limited traversal for the graph and the scorer (SD-057).
FL-015.walk: Open the Memory Graph on a curated memory; typed edges (merged from, supersedes, contradicts) are drawn to its relatives.

FL-026.label: The keyword, project key and origin path columns on a memory are filled in and factored into scoring.
FL-026.walk: Open a memory card; keyword, project and origin path are filled, and the score breakdown shows them counting.

FL-034.label: The curators deconflict, dedupe and remove slop, triggered by every n memory writes rather than by the clock, and run at the Palace's own location.
FL-034.walk: Add 25 memories to a palace holding near-duplicates; a curator pass runs on its own (every 25 admitted writes or 3 gate removals), finds the pair by near-identical relevance scores on the standard probe set as well as by embedding, and proposes one lossless combined memory; Palace State shows the pass and the palace's growth curve bending; a compaction's admitted facts trigger a pass too, merging them with what the Palace already holds (owner, 2026-10-05, v2.133).

FL-035.label: Constitution: A scripted pre-pass that writes a versioned Palace Health Report the curator must read before acting (v2.8–2.9 curator law).
FL-035.walk: Run a curator pass; its record shows the Palace Health Report it read first.

FL-036.label: The curators have the right tools and standard procedures for their work, and act as surgeons: minimally invasive, targeting the root problem and letting the system sort out the symptoms.
FL-036.walk: Run a curator pass on a Palace with one duplicate pair; the pass touches only that pair and nothing else.

FL-037.label: Constitution: Typed consolidation decisions: merge, new, contradict, supersede (curator spec).
FL-037.walk: Open a curator merge card: it shows the lossless combined memory beside its sources; approve, amend the text, or give feedback (which is recorded as a tuning signal); a typed merge / new / contradict / supersede verdict is visible on the card (owner, 2026-09-30).

FL-038.label: A cheap 80/20 duplicate check at memory creation, keeping the agent's memory work under 10% of build run time.
FL-038.walk: Save a fact already in the Palace: at cosine 0.92 or above the save comes back 'already known — reinforced' at once, between 0.80 and 0.92 it asks to confirm, without the agent reading other memories; these write-time bands are the C.4 defaults and are separate from the curator's own search band (v2.128).

FL-041.label: Constitution: Curator autonomy earned per verdict class from your own approval record, with contradiction never graduating (gate-day).
FL-041.walk: Open Palace State; each verdict class shows whether it has graduated to auto-execute, and contradiction never does.

FL-042.label: Constitution: 'Already known — reinforced' on re-saves; rejected candidates remembered and never re-proposed without material change (gate-day).
FL-042.walk: Re-save a known fact; the reply says 'already known — reinforced'; reject a candidate and re-save it unchanged; it is not proposed again.

FL-045.label: Same-memory detection by encoding and retrieving, not exact wording.
FL-045.walk: Save a rephrased known fact: at 0.80 similarity or above it is recognized at once (asked or reinforced, per the write bands) instead of duplicating; a rewording below 0.80 is saved, and the next curator pass proposes merging the pair (its own 0.70 band, v2.128).

FL-109.label: Memory candidates appear under the agent's post on the Deck after a compaction or a thread close; scrolling past without denying approves them; corpus-born proposals live in Memory Ingest.
FL-109.walk: After a compaction, candidates appear under the post; scroll past; they are approved and land.

FL-114.label: Memory Ingest as its own module: put in current AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md files to jump-start the Palace.
FL-114.walk: Put an AGENTS.md into the Memory Ingest module; its contents show up as memory candidates.

FL-169.label: Client and cloud versions stay sync-locked or backward compatible, following industry practice, so version differences feel seamless.
FL-169.walk: Start a client whose version differs from the cloud Palace's; it either keeps working or refuses with a plain version message.

FL-178.label: Constitution: a verification identity with its own account and home for tests and scouts (gate verification-identity work).
FL-178.walk: Start the daemon as the verification identity; its Palace shows none of the owner's memories.

FL-179.label: Constitution: a plain ownership refusal when one identity tries to decide another identity's approval queue item (gate verification-identity work).
FL-179.walk: As the verification identity, decide a card in the owner's approval queue; a plain refusal appears.

FL-003.label: Constitution: Every edit is a compare-and-swap revision, deletions are tombstones, and a write conflict is a first-class event (founding ADRs).
FL-003.walk: Edit a memory body; the memory shows a new revision and the old revision is still retrievable.

FL-080.label: Compaction triggered by fill percentage against the model's best working range and max, which vary by model.
FL-080.walk: Fill a thread past its model's fill line; compaction runs and the fill percentage drops.

FL-133.label: A corner palace view with curators as ghosts moving through the database.
FL-133.walk: Open the separate Palace module during a real curator pass; ghost-like curators move between the feed's actual finding targets before the pass finishes. LOOK (v2.119): the module is judged beside its plate (palace.png) — same material, structure and density; the side-by-side capture is required.

FL-162.label: Easy onboarding from a single splash repo, needing only two secrets: a GCP credential and an OpenRouter key.
FL-162.walk: On a fresh machine, follow the splash repo's install steps; you are asked for a GCP credential and an OpenRouter key and nothing else before the app comes up.

FL-163.label: Seed ingestion at startup: upload markdown files (or the machine's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md) and the curators break them into individual memories.
FL-163.walk: M3WF fixture: focus Memory Ingest’s drop/paste control and paste a two-fact fictional Markdown document; review the individual split memories. A native file chooser is optional.

FL-164.label: Local mode with no internet, cloud mode, and a way to mirror our cloud setup into your own provider.
FL-164.walk: M3WF fixture (harness/verification/m3wf/README.md): Start the Harness with the network off and send one message; the reply arrives and the memory lands in the local palace.

FL-167.label: One obvious start command with an update prompt; update, deploy, launch and doctor as one or two commands.
FL-167.walk: M3WF fixture (harness/verification/m3wf/README.md): Run the one start command when a newer release exists; it offers the update, then launches.

FL-182.label: Agent workflows that are programmable, so making agents do work is extremely easy.
FL-182.walk: Save an agent workflow and run it twice; both runs do the same work without a person steering.
